```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Available on CRAN
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(magrittr)
library(ruv)
library(tibble)
library(janitor)
library(tidyr)
library(ggpubr)

# Available on Bioconductor
library(NanoTube)
```

```{r}
sample_metadata_filepath <- "/root/capsule/data/tak188-mouse-preclinical-nanostring-v2/"
rcc_filepath <- "/root/capsule/data/tak188-mouse-preclinical-nanostring-v2"
```

# Read in data

```{r}
sample_info <- read.csv(file.path(sample_metadata_filepath, "20260408_metadata.csv"))
# Add a 'replicate' column to sample_info
sample_info %<>%
   group_by(treatment, day) %>%
   mutate(replicate = row_number()) %>%
   ungroup()

# List all files with .RCC extension in the specified directory
rcc_files <- list.files(rcc_filepath, 
                  pattern = "\\.RCC$", 
                  full.names = TRUE)

# First two lines viewing RCC as text file

# FileVersion,1.7 SoftwareVersion,6.0.2
# ID,01 Owner, Comments, Date,20260408 GeneRLF,NS_Mm_IO_360_v1.0 SystemAPF,n6_vDV1 ID,12 FovCount,280 FovCounted,280 ScannerID,2212E0093 StagePosition,1 BindingDensity,1.46 CartridgeID,day 10 CartridgeBarcode, 

```

# QC failed

Sample "day 14_01_06" clearly must be removed per previous QC.

```{r}
rcc_files <- c(rcc_files[1:17], rcc_files[19:23])
sample_info %<>% filter(file_name != "20260408_day 14_01_06.RCC")

rcc_d10 <- rcc_files[1:12]
rcc_d14 <- rcc_files[13:22]
```

## Positive control normalization factor

The last QC has to be done after PC normalization. Run without HKG normalization to set up for evaluating pre-normalization HKG expression. 

```{r}
dat <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = rcc_files, 
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE,
                  skip.housekeeping = TRUE)

dat_d10 <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = rcc_d10, 
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE,
                  skip.housekeeping = TRUE
                  )

dat_d14 <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = rcc_d14, 
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE, 
                  skip.housekeeping = TRUE
                  )
```

```{r}
# Positive control
posQC <- positiveQC(dat)$tab %>%
   clean_names() %>%
   remove_rownames()

posQC_d10 <- positiveQC(dat_d10)$tab %>%
   clean_names() %>%
   remove_rownames()

posQC_d14 <- positiveQC(dat_d14)$tab %>%
   clean_names() %>%
   remove_rownames()
```


```{r}
posQC %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = scale_factor)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Positive control normalization factor") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.3, color = "red", size = 1) +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 3, color = "red", size = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

All samples in range 

```{r}
posQC_d10 %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = scale_factor)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Positive control normalization factor") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.3, color = "red", size = 1) +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 3, color = "red", size = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   ggtitle("Day 10 samples only (separately processed)")
```

All samples in range

```{r}
posQC_d14 %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = scale_factor)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Positive control normalization factor") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.3, color = "red", size = 1) +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 3, color = "red", size = 1) +
```

All samples in range.

# Inspecting HKG expression
## Endogenous genes

```{r}
data.frame(dat$exprs) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column("Accession") %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict) %>% select(Accession, Name, CodeClass), by = "Accession") %>%
   filter(CodeClass == "Endogenous") %>%
   pivot_longer(cols = -c(Accession, Name, CodeClass), names_to = "sample", values_to = "expr") %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = expr)) +
   geom_boxplot() +
   ggtitle("Overall expression level of endogenous genes") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   xlab("Expression level (no HKG normalized)") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   scale_x_log10()
```

Extreme bimodality in overall expression of genes.

## Calculate which are above background

Assume we are setting background for each sample as the mean of the negative controls, 
and calculate whether genes are above this background level.

```{r genedata, eval=T}
gene_names <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(CodeClass %in% c("Housekeeping", "Endogenous")) %>% pull(Accession)
hkg_gene_names <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(CodeClass == "Housekeeping") %>% pull(Accession)

# Extract HKG counts
hkg_counts <- dat$exprs[hkg_gene_names, ]
hkg_counts_d10 <- dat_d10$exprs[hkg_gene_names, ]
hkg_counts_d14 <- dat_d14$exprs[hkg_gene_names, ]

# Extract negative control counts 
negative_control_names <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(CodeClass == "Negative") %>% pull(Accession)
negative_control_counts <- dat$exprs[negative_control_names, ]
negative_control_counts <- data.frame(negative_control_counts) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Accession") %>%
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict), by = "Accession") %>%
   relocate(Name) %>% select(-CodeClass)
negative_control_counts %<>% pivot_longer(-c(Name, Accession), names_to = "sample", values_to = "count")
negative_control_counts <- data.frame(negative_control_counts) %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict), by = c("Accession", "Name")) %>%
   relocate(Name) %>% select(-CodeClass)
negQC <- negativeQC(dat, interactive.plot = FALSE)$tab %>%
   clean_names() %>%
   rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
   mutate(genes_below_bg_count = as.integer(sub(" \\(.*\\)", "", genes_below_bg_percent)),
          genes_below_bg_percent = as.numeric(sub(".*\\((.*)%\\)", "\\1", genes_below_bg_percent)))

# Extract positive control counts
positive_control_names <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(CodeClass == "Positive") %>% pull(Accession)
positive_control_counts <- dat$exprs[positive_control_names, ]
positive_control_counts <- data.frame(positive_control_counts) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Accession") %>%
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict), by = "Accession") %>%
   relocate(Name) %>% select(-CodeClass)
positive_control_counts %<>% pivot_longer(-c(Name, Accession), names_to = "sample", values_to = "count")

# Control dataframe

controls_df <- positive_control_counts %>% 
   filter(Name == "POS_E(0.5)") %>% 
   select(sample, pos_E = count) %>%
   left_join(negative_control_counts %>% 
               group_by(sample) %>% 
               summarize(negative_control_mean = mean(count), 
                         negative_control_sd = sd(count)), by = "sample") %>%
   mutate(positive_control_lod = (pos_E - negative_control_mean)/negative_control_sd) %>% 
   left_join(positive_control_counts %>% 
   filter(Name == "POS_A(128)") %>% 
   select(sample, pos_A = count), by = "sample")

qc_data_gene <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(CodeClass %in% c("Housekeeping")) 

# percent of samples above background for each gene
qc_data_gene$pct_above_background <- apply(X = hkg_counts, MARGIN = 1, 
      function(x) sum(x > controls_df$negative_control_mean)/nrow(controls_df) * 100)
```


## Identify which HKG are above background

```{r, eval=T}
qc_data_gene %>% filter(CodeClass == "Housekeeping") %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = Name, x = pct_above_background)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("% of samples above negative-control background") +
   ylab("Gene name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 100, color = "red", size = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Without HKG normalization (all samples processed together), 
HKGs are not all above background (mean of negative controls) in all samples.


```{r}
hkg_counts  %>%
   data.frame() %>% 
   rownames_to_column("Accession") %>%
   pivot_longer(cols = -Accession, names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict) %>% filter(CodeClass == "Housekeeping") %>% select(Accession, Name), by = c("Accession")) %>% 
   mutate(sample = gsub("^X", "", sample),
          sample = gsub("day.", "day ", sample, fixed=T)) %>%
   left_join(negQC %>% select(sample, mean_neg), by = "sample") %>%
   mutate(negQC_pass = count > mean_neg) %>%
   ggplot(aes(x = sample, y = log10(count), color = negQC_pass)) +
   geom_point() +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   coord_flip()
```

There are two groups of samples with different ranges of HKG expression. Some have about half of them below negative control mean.


## Expression level and confounding factors

Check HKG association with treatment/other metadata and see whether counts are above 100 (or 20 if need be)

```{r hkglevel2, eval=T}
hkg_counts  %>%
   data.frame() %>% 
   rownames_to_column("Accession") %>%
   pivot_longer(cols = -Accession, names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict) %>% filter(CodeClass == "Housekeeping") %>% select(Accession, Name), by = c("Accession")) %>% 
   mutate(sample = gsub("^X", "", sample),
          sample = gsub("day.", "day ", sample, fixed=T)) %>%
   left_join(sample_info, by = c("sample" = "file_name")) %>%
   ggplot(aes(x = as.character(day), y = log10(count))) +
   geom_boxplot() +
   facet_wrap(~Name) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   stat_compare_means(method = "t.test", label = "p.signif") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = log10(100), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = log10(20), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
   ggtitle("All samples (no HKG norm, processed together)")
```

D14 is significantly higher.  

```{r hkglevel3, eval=T}
hkg_counts_d10  %>%
   data.frame() %>% 
   rownames_to_column("Accession") %>%
   pivot_longer(cols = -Accession, names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict) %>% filter(CodeClass == "Housekeeping") %>% select(Accession, Name), by = c("Accession")) %>% 
   mutate(sample = gsub("^X", "", sample),
          sample = gsub("day.", "day ", sample, fixed=T)) %>%
   left_join(sample_info, by = c("sample" = "file_name")) %>%
   filter(day == 10) %>%
   ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = log10(count))) +
   geom_boxplot() +
   facet_wrap(~Name) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   stat_compare_means(method = "t.test", label = "p.signif") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = log10(100), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = log10(20), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
   ggtitle("Day 10 samples only (separately processed, no HKG norm)")
```

There is no significant difference (nominal t-test p-value) between the treatments in any HKG expression at D10, processed separately.

```{r hkglevel4, eval=T}
hkg_counts_d14  %>%
   data.frame() %>% 
   rownames_to_column("Accession") %>%
   pivot_longer(cols = -Accession, names_to = "sample", values_to = "count") %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat$dict) %>% filter(CodeClass == "Housekeeping") %>% select(Accession, Name), by = c("Accession")) %>% 
   mutate(sample = gsub("^X", "", sample),
          sample = gsub("day.", "day ", sample, fixed=T)) %>%
   left_join(sample_info, by = c("sample" = "file_name")) %>%
   filter(day == 14) %>%
   ggplot(aes(x = treatment, y = log10(count))) +
   geom_boxplot() +
   facet_wrap(~Name) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   stat_compare_means(method = "t.test", label = "p.signif") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = log10(100), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = log10(20), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
   ggtitle("Day 14 samples only (separately normalized)")
```

There is no significant difference (nominal t-test p-value) between the treatments in any 
HKG expression at D14, processed separately. 
Two samples have much lower expression of everything (07 and 02).

## Calculate variance of each HKG

```{r hkgvariance, eval=T}
# Skipping


hkg_variance <- qc_data_gene %>%
   filter(CodeClass == "Housekeeping") %>%
   mutate(variance = apply(X = hkg_counts[rownames(.),], MARGIN = 1, FUN = var),
          mean = apply(X = hkg_counts[rownames(.),], MARGIN = 1, FUN = mean))

# Choose a set of housekeeping genes with similar variance

# Visualize the variance of housekeeping genes
hkg_variance %>%
   ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Name, variance), y = variance)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Housekeeping Gene") +
   ylab("Variance") +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
   geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(hkg_variance$variance, 0.25), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = quantile(hkg_variance$variance, 0.75), color = "blue", linetype = "dashed")
```

## Identify HKG with low expression or expressed in fewer samples

Omit some for normalization due to lower than 100 mean expression (pre normalization) 
or expressed above mean negative control in less than ~80% of samples.

```{r hkg_omit}
omit_hkg <- c("Mrpl19", "Nrde2", "Tlk2", "Ubb", # low expression, potentially missingness
"Ercc3", "Sf3a1", "Tlk2", "Dnajc14" # missingness
)
omit_hkg_names <- data.frame(dat$dict) %>%
   filter(Name %in% omit_hkg) %>% pull(Accession)
use_hkg_names <- setdiff(hkg_gene_names, omit_hkg_names)
```

# HKG normalization with 13 genes

```{r}
dat_hk <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = rcc_files, 
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE,
                  housekeeping = use_hkg_names)

dat_d10_hk <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = rcc_d10, 
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE,
                  housekeeping = use_hkg_names)

dat_d14_hk <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = rcc_d14, 
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE, 
                  housekeeping = use_hkg_names)
```

## HKG normalization factor

Manufacturer recommends additional caution for samples with scale factors outside the range of 0.1-10.

```{r}
data.frame(dat_hk$hk.scalefactors) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = dat_hk.hk.scalefactors)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Housekeeping gene normalization factor") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, color = "red", size = 1) +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 10, color = "red", size = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12)
```

Processed+normalized both days together: samples are either ~0 (mostly D10) or 2 (mostly D14).

```{r}
data.frame(dat_d10_hk$hk.scalefactors) %>%

```

Day 10 alone: 3 samples high; rest are low. 6 of the low are below desired range.

```{r}
data.frame(dat_d14_hk$hk.scalefactors) %>%
```

# PC
## All
All samples processed together, HKG normalization 13 genes.
Manual inspection using interactive plot:
d10 05 is outlier in PC1 (43% var) and d14 09 is outlier in PC2 (27% var).  

```{r eval=T}
p <- nanostringPCA(dat_hk, interactive.plot = T)$pca
nanostringPCA(dat_hk, interactive.plot = T)$plt
```

Samples clearly cluster in PC1 by HKG normalization factor, which generally splits by day.

```{r eval=T}
data.frame(p$x) %>%
   rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
   left_join(sample_info, by = c("sample" = "file_name")) %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat_hk$hk.scalefactors) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column("sample")) %>% 
   ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = dat_hk.hk.scalefactors, shape = as.character(day))) +
   geom_point(size = 3) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   ggtitle("All samples processed together") +
   scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red")
```

## D10 
D10 samples alone, HKG normalization 13 genes. 
Manual inspection using interactive plot:
d10 05 is separated from the rest in PC1 which is 55% of the variance. 
The three samples with low normalization factor (01, 02, 12) are at one side of PC1 but not separated. 
PC2 has two groups not considering 05 (11% var).

```{r eval=T}
p <- nanostringPCA(dat_d10_hk, interactive.plot = T)$pca

nanostringPCA(dat_d10_hk, interactive.plot = T)$plt
```

PC1 is normalization factor. Not sure what is driving PC2, it's not treatment.

```{r eval=T}
data.frame(p$x) %>%
   rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
   left_join(sample_info, by = c("sample" = "file_name")) %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat_d10_hk$hk.scalefactors) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column("sample")) %>% 
   ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = dat_d10_hk$hk.scalefactors, shape = treatment)) +
   geom_point(size = 3) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   ggtitle("D10") +
   scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red")
```

## D14
D14 samples normalized. 
Manual inspection using interactive plot:
PC1 has 09 as an outlier with 47% of the variance. 
02 and 07 are very separated from the rest in PC2 which is 29% of the variance. Those are the samples with low HKG norm factor.

```{r eval=T}
p <- nanostringPCA(dat_d14_hk, interactive.plot = T)$pca

nanostringPCA(dat_d14_hk, interactive.plot = T)$plt
```

PC1 and PC2 are both associated with HKG normalization factor, which is not surprising given the large variance explained by PC1 and the outliers in PC1 and PC2 being the samples with low HKG normalization factor. Treatment does not appear to be associated with either of the PCs.
```{r eval=T}
data.frame(p$x) %>%
   rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
   left_join(sample_info, by = c("sample" = "file_name")) %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat_d14_hk$hk.scalefactors) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column("sample")) %>% 
   ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = dat_d14_hk$hk.scalefactors, shape = treatment)) +
   geom_point(size = 3) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   ggtitle("D14") +
   scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red")
```

# Filtering outliers and re-running normalization

## D10

Normalization factors might be ok. Remove 5 due to PC outlier.

D10: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 [control] 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 [treatment]

## D14

Remaining if we take out normalization factor (2, 7) and PCA (9) outliers
D14: 1, 3, 4, 5, [control] 8, 10, 11 [treatment]

```{r}
dat_d14_filter <- processNanostringData(
                  nsFiles = c(rcc_d14[1], rcc_d14[3:5], rcc_d14[7], rcc_d14[9:10]),
                  normalization='nSolver',
                  output.format = "list", 
                  includeQC = TRUE, 
                  housekeeping = use_hkg_names
               )
hkQC_d14_filter <- data.frame(hk_scale_factor = dat_d14_filter$hk.scalefactors) %>% 
      rownames_to_column("sample")
```

```{r}
hkQC_d14_filter %>%
   ggplot(aes(y = sample, x = hk_scale_factor)) +
   geom_col() +
   xlab("Housekeeping gene normalization factor") +
   ylab("Sample name") +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, color = "red", size = 1) +
   geom_vline(xintercept = 10, color = "red", size = 1) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   ggtitle("Day 14 samples only")
```

All normalization factors are in the same range.

```{r eval=T}
p <- nanostringPCA(dat_d14_filter, interactive.plot = T)$pca

nanostringPCA(dat_d14_filter, interactive.plot = T)$plt
```

PC1 and PC2 are both associated with HKG normalization factor, which is not surprising given the large variance explained by PC1 and the outliers in PC1 and PC2 being the samples with low HKG normalization factor. Treatment does not appear to be associated with either of the PCs.
```{r eval=T}
data.frame(p$x) %>%
   rownames_to_column("sample") %>%
   left_join(sample_info, by = c("sample" = "file_name")) %>% 
   left_join(data.frame(dat_d14_filter$hk.scalefactors) %>% 
   tibble::rownames_to_column("sample")) %>% 
   ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = dat_d14_filter$hk.scalefactors, shape = treatment)) +
   geom_point(size = 3) +
   theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
   ggtitle("D14 (filter out outliers)") +
   scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red")
```

Unremarkable PCA
